# The Estate Organiser (Australian Edition)

> The Estate Organiser is a fill-in-the-blanks workbook for Australian families. You write down where everything is kept: bank accounts, super funds, insurance policies, where the passwords live, funeral wishes, final instructions. Then the person who has to sort it all out one day is not left guessing. It is not an app and it is not a cloud service. The printed edition is a coil bound book you fill in by hand. The digital edition is a fillable file that stays on your own computer. What you write is never stored on our servers. The Organiser is a record-keeping tool. It is not legal, financial or tax advice, and it does not replace a Will or the work a solicitor does. It sits alongside those documents. Operated by Prestige Worldwright Pty Ltd (ABN 46 691 517 692). Canadian and American editions are published separately.

- [The Estate Organiser](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/): what the book is, what sits inside it, and why a Will on its own leaves gaps.

- [Advance Care Directive QLD: The Advance Health Directive Explained](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/advance-care-directive-qld/): Queensland's advance health directive (Form 4): who signs, who can witness and where to send it.

- [Executor of a Will in Australia: Duties and Checklist](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/executor-checklist-australia/): what an executor is, whether an executor can be a beneficiary, and the full job in order.
- [What Should I Leave for My Family So They Can Find Everything?](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/what-to-leave-for-your-family-australia/): a single written map of where everything is kept, so your family is not left guessing.
- [How to Get Your Affairs in Order in Australia: A Checklist](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/get-your-affairs-in-order-australia/): six practical jobs, with the power of attorney document names for each state and territory.
- [Where Should You Keep Your Will in Australia?](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/where-to-keep-your-will-australia/): why the signed original matters and the usual places to store it.
- [What Is Probate in Australia? How Long It Takes and What It Costs](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/what-is-probate-australia/): what probate is, how long it takes in each state, and every state's court filing fee from 1 July 2026.
- [What Does an Executor Actually Do in Australia?](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/what-does-an-executor-do-australia/): the real duties that land on an executor.
- [Just Became an Executor? What to Do in the First Few Weeks](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/executor-first-steps-checklist/): the first steps, in order, for someone who has just taken the job on.
- [What Happens If You Die Without a Will in Australia?](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/dying-without-a-will-australia/): how intestacy works and who decides what happens.
- [Does a Will Cover Everything? What Sits Outside It](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/does-a-will-cover-everything-australia/): the assets a Will does not control.
- [What Happens to Your Super When You Die in Australia?](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/what-happens-to-super-when-you-die-australia/): why superannuation is handled separately from the rest of an estate.
- [Binding Death Benefit Nomination: How It Works in Australia](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/death-benefit-nomination-australia/): who you can nominate, the two-witness rule and why many binding nominations lapse after 3 years.
- [Power of Attorney vs a Will: What Is the Difference?](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/power-of-attorney-vs-will-australia/): what each document does and when each one applies.
- [What Happens to Your Online Accounts When You Die?](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/online-accounts-passwords-when-you-die/): digital accounts, password access and the safe way to leave instructions.
- [Funeral Wishes: The Conversation Worth Having Early](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/funeral-wishes-conversation/): how to write down what you want before anyone has to guess.
- [How to Talk to Your Parents About Their Estate Plans](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/talk-to-parents-about-estate-plans/): opening lines for a conversation most families put off.
- [What to Do When Someone Dies: A Checklist for Australia](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/what-to-do-when-someone-dies-australia/): the first hours, the first week, the first month. Who to call, how the death gets registered, who has to be told, and what can wait. Australian government sources for every step.
- [Probate Checklist Australia: How to Apply, State by State](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/probate-checklist-australia/): the order you apply for probate in Australia: publish the notice of intention, wait out your state's period, then file. The waiting periods, the filing systems and the court fees for all eight states and territories.
- [How to Organise Important Documents for Your Family If You Die](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/how-to-organise-important-documents-australia/): the documents an Australian family gets asked for, which ones only work if you make them in advance, where each one lives, and how to keep the set current. With the government sources for each.
- [What to Organise Before a Parent Dies: An Australian Checklist](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/what-to-organise-before-a-parent-dies/): several of the documents that matter can only be made while a parent still has decision-making capacity. What to organise while that window is open, with the state by state differences and the government sources for each.
- [SS524 Form: How an Executor Gets Information from Centrelink](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/ss524-form-executor-centrelink/): Form SS524 lets an executor or administrator ask Services Australia about a deceased person's Centrelink payments and debts. Who can use it and what to send.
- [Australian Death Notification Service: How It Works](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/australian-death-notification-service/): The Australian Death Notification Service lets an executor tell participating banks, super funds and other organisations about a death in one free online notice.
- [Financial Information Service (FIS): Free Help from Services Australia](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/financial-information-service-centrelink/): The Financial Information Service is a free, confidential Services Australia service that explains money matters such as retirement, aged care and inheritances.
- [Carer Payment After the Person You Care For Dies](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/carer-payment-after-death/): if you get Carer Payment and the person you care for dies, it may continue for up to 14 weeks. Lump sums, Carer Allowance and the 28-day rule, explained.
- [Centrelink Gifting Rules: $10,000 a Year, $30,000 over 5 Years](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/centrelink-gifting-rules/): Centrelink's gifting free areas are $10,000 a financial year and $30,000 over 5 financial years. What happens above that, and before the house goes in the kids' names.
- [Inheritance and the Age Pension: Tell Centrelink Within 14 Days](https://www.theestateorganiser.com.au/blog/inheritance-age-pension-centrelink/): Services Australia says you must tell it within 14 days of getting assets or income from a deceased estate. How an inheritance can affect the Age Pension and the Pensioner Concession Card.
